channel.title: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Iran nuclear inspections, deadly church attack in Jordan, El Fasher – one year on
item.description: The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, called on Friday for a swift return of inspectors to Iran, warning of growing fragility in the global nuclear non-proliferation regime.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Blood brothers: WHO chief joins ENHYPEN to celebrate drive success
item.description: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) is a self-confessed fan of K-pop sensation ENHYPEN and this week, he got the chance to tell them so in person.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
item.description: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan: Drone strikes killed at least 306 people in three weeks
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Friday strongly condemned an escalation in drone strikes across Sudan this month, which killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October alone.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Soil mapping aims to boost agricultural production in Kenya
item.description: A new Kenyan initiative is helping farmers better understand their soils in a bid to improve crop yields amid intensifying climate shocks.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Burden and loss’ builds in DR Congo, as Kenya strengthens Ebola containment
item.description: As Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), more resources are needed to fight the disease and feed patients and families, UN agencies said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
item.description: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Russian attacks intensify, UN team tours West Bank, ‘unlawful’ elderly deaths
item.description: Long-range Russian attacks across Ukraine are intensifying, including in Kyiv, causing at least 14 civilian deaths and 78 injuries overnight into Thursday, as UN agencies continue to provide aid.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: First human case of Shamonda virus reported in France as patient dies
item.description: A patient in France has died after being infected with Shamonda virus, the first recorded human case of the disease.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal’s deadly glacier flood a ‘defining moment’ for the international community
item.description: The deadly flash flood that tore through Nepal in August is a “defining moment” for both the country and the international community, according to the head of the UN field agency which builds roads, schools and clinics in crisis zones.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Mothers get nearly eight times more paid leave than fathers – and women pay the price
item.description: Mothers around the world get nearly eight times as much paid leave as fathers, leaving women to shoulder most of the care burden – at a cost to families, children and economies, according to new UN data published on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: DR Congo: Ebola responders under pressure as outbreak expands
item.description: As the deadly Ebola disease outbreak reached an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), investigators pursued all leads on Thursday to assess the risk of the disease spreading in Nigeria.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Connect the dots’ between street protests and global turmoil, urges Guterres
item.description: The international community must combat inequality and stop wars from expanding to ensure a safer world for all, the UN Secretary-General said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Fate unknown of many returned to DPR Korea from China: UN independent experts
item.description: Three years on from the reported resumption of large-scale forcible returns of nationals of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) from China, serious concerns persist about their fate, according to a group of Human Rights Council-appointed independent experts.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Ominous start’ to West Bank olive harvest amid settler attacks
item.description: The use of live ammunition, arson and the destruction of centuries-old olive trees have marked the opening weeks of this year’s harvest in the occupied West Bank.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Aid for Ethiopia, Abyei drone strikes condemned, extreme heat and newborn health
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) is scaling up emergency health response operations across Afar, Amhara and Tigray in Ethiopia to address growing humanitarian and health needs resulting from ongoing hostilities.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes
item.description: The price tag for smuggling on European sea routes reached up to half a billion dollars last year, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Summit in Samarkand, a boon for child wellbeing and health
item.description: Representatives from across the international community are meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to ensure that children everywhere can thrive in a world marred by war, climate chaos and other fundamental challenges.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN agencies appeal for help to protect weakest from unprecedented El Niño
item.description: Two UN agencies issued a powerful appeal on Wednesday for immediate assistance to help communities already being impacted by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
item.description: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: WHO supports Nigeria after first Ebola case confirmed
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) is assisting Nigeria following confirmation of the first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back
item.description: With global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, countries “must pull out all the stops” and urgently cut emissions to minimize the overshoot and return to the internationally agreed threshold by the end of this century.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI on track to ‘crowd out’ human decision-making in warfare
item.description: Artificial intelligence is already being widely used on the battlefield, and the role of human judgment in military operations is shrinking rapidly, the head of the UN’s independent disarmament research institute warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As Sudan war spills into Central African Republic, UN warns against early peacekeeper exit
item.description: The UN warned on Tuesday against a premature withdrawal of its peacekeepers as the war in Sudan spills over into the Central African Republic (CAR).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Bangladesh: UNICEF chief calls for an end to child marriage
item.description: At 14, Bushra faced being married off – until community leaders at a UNICEF-supported child protection hub worked with her father to prevent her from being given away against her will.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘One step away from famine’: Inside Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
item.description: Following extreme hunger warnings, a bitter reality is unfolding across Afghanistan: food is available, but remains inaccessible for millions of people.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
item.description: More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
item.description: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
item.description: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
item.description: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
